transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Cho (Redwood GTM), Mark Holden (StratusAI - Head of Alliances), Lina Gomez (Partner Sales Lead), Ibrahim Khan (Solutions Architect)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check—can you see my screen? I pulled the draft co-sell worksheet and a one-pager for the sprint.

[00:12] Mark: Yep, seeing it. Thanks Alex. We got Lina and I on this side, and Ibrahim is dialed in from the east coast.

[00:20] Priya: Cool. I wanna be explicit up front — goal for this call is to agree on how we route, qualify, and pilot three joint accounts over the next 6 weeks. Sound right?

[00:30] Lina: Yes. We have a couple of marketing events looming so we also want to scope what assets we need.

[00:36] Alex: Great. So first slide — ownership model. We propose a shared tracker where Stratus logs inbound leads and Redwood tags product-fit level A/B/C plus model preference. Then we route based on lead score.

[00:50] Mark: How do you define product-fit A? For us, A means customer is actively evaluating inference infra, has >$100k ARR potential and needs VPC or dedicated options.

[01:06] Alex: That aligns well. Our suggested A is: production LLM usage required, privacy/regulatory needs or SLA requests, and ACV over $75k. B is pilotable but not immediate spend. C is marketing nurture.

[01:20] Ibrahim: Quick technical question — when you say \"dedicated\" how strict is the requirement on VPC? A lot of our customers want private tenancy or on-prem.

[01:30] Priya: Good point. Redwood Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools and our Private deploy supports VPC or on-prem installs. For pilots we'll usually start hosted for speed unless data residency or SOC2 controls require Private.

[01:44] Ibrahim: Ok. And about latency — we had a lead concerned about kv cache performance on long context windows.

[01:52] Priya: (laughs) We sometimes see \"kay vee cash\" in notes — that's KV cache. Our baseline tests will include 8k and 32k context runs; we'll capture p99 latency and token cost.

[02:05] Sam: On the GTM side, the ask is simple: for A deals Stratus owns initial conversation and Redwood supports with SE + pricing. For B deals we want a joint outreach with Stratus listing the partner value-add.

[02:18] Mark: Works. Question — revenue split discussion? Our legal wants a simple referral fee on the first year and then a smaller sharing if we close more deeply.

[02:28] Alex: We can do a referral -> motion where initial introduction yields a finder fee (standard percentage), then for larger deals we move to an MSA addendum with co-sell terms. I can share a template, but legal will need to confirm.

[02:40] Lina: Please share the template. Also, do you have any measurement for how Redwood credits leads when there are multiple touches? Our CRM processes need that.

[02:52] Alex: We'll use first-touch in the tracker but can flag when Redwood expands the opportunity to full close and then update attribution. We can add a column for 'owner at close' in the sheet.

[03:03] Mark: Makes sense. Let's switch to the pilot plan — Priya?

[03:08] Priya: Sure. Technical pilot is two parts: 1) a quick functional demo and 2) a 1-week benchmark. For benchmark we collect throughput/latency, cost per 1k tokens, and stability under a ~2k qps simulation for a short burst. We'll also test prefix caching for conversational flows.

[03:26] Ibrahim: For the qps sim — do you simulate streaming and non-streaming? Many customers stream to reduce perceived latency.

[03:32] Priya: We'll include both. Streaming adds complexity, and we'll measure end-to-end TTFF (time to first token) and time-to-complete for 1k token responses.

[03:44] Mark: Any restrictions on datasets for benchmarking? Some customers won't share production prompts.

[03:50] Priya: We can use synthetic prompts or a sanitized prompt set. The important part is distribution shape — avg length, tail length percentiles. We can also run with the customer's anonymous prompts if they prefer.

[03:59] Alex: For timeline, proposal: Mark picks three opportunities this week — ideally a mix (1 enterprise SOC2-heavy, 1 mid-market chat use-case, 1 ISV embedding use-case). Then Priya runs two pilot benchmarks (one hosted baseline, one dedicated/private if customer needs). Priya, can you do those in the week of 4/14?

[04:18] Priya: Yes, that works. I’ll need access to sample prompts and an estimated seq length distribution. Also an AE owner on the customer side to help with signoff for load tests.

[04:30] Mark: Lina will coordinate on the sample sets. Ibrahim will help prepare the sandbox for the one on-prem trial.

[04:36] Lina: We'll also want a short joint one-pager for sales enablement — message map, key objection handling (latency vs cost), and the co-sell pitch.

[04:46] Sam: We have a templated one-pager; Alex will customize per deal. Also we'll need to track content approvals for any co-branded assets — legal review can take 5-7 business days.

[04:58] Alex: Noted. I'll push the draft to the drive and add approvers.

[05:03] Mark: On the CRM side — can we set up a shared opportunity pipeline in a spreadsheet? We want to track stage, expected ACV, next step, Redwood owner, Stratus owner, and handoff triggers.

[05:14] Alex: Yes — I'll share the co-sell tracker. The rules: when an opportunity hits 'SOW requested' stage, Redwood AE takes lead on pricing, Stratus stays as partner of record for credit unless Redwood expands scope.

[05:28] Ibrahim: A quick compliance question — for prospects in EU we need data residency and DSAR handling. Do you have EU regions and specific logs for audit?

[05:37] Priya: We operate in multiple regions and can deploy Private in a customer's VPC. We also have audit logging and key management integrations (KMS). For enterprise we can do dedicated logging and longer retention in the console.

[05:50] Lina: Are there any limitations on model variants in Private? One of our ISV prospects uses a very large open backbone that might require custom kernels.

[05:59] Priya: Most open models we support; custom kernels sometimes need additional validation. For the pilot we can run the variant in hosted or dedicated and then move to Private after a short onboarding if needed. We'll flag any performance caveats up front.

[06:12] Alex: Let's cover event co-sell briefly — Stratus suggested co-sponsoring a webinar on \"Inference economics: balancing latency & cost.\" Lina, do you have dates?

[06:21] Lina: We have a slot the week of 5/12 at the vendor summit. We could do a 30-min joint talk and then a 1:1 demo booth.

[06:29] Sam: Perfect. Redwood can provide a demo rig and a short case study. Will need marketing contacts to coordinate collateral.

[06:35] Mark: We'll also want an intro plan for the top account — who does the outreach and what's the messaging?

[06:40] Alex: Suggested approach: Stratus does intro call, then Redwood SE joins for a technical deep-dive. We'll prep a two-slide impact deck showing latency/cost delta and the pilot plan.

[06:50] Ibrahim: For the deep-dive — can we focus on three KPIs: p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and failure rate under burst? If we get those numbers in one pager it helps procurement.

[06:58] Priya: Absolutely. We'll produce a KPI table.

[07:02] (background noise)

[07:15] Mark: Switching briefly — competition. We've heard from a couple of customers that CloudEndpoint Co. is pushing an easier pricing story, and VertigoAI is touting embeddings performance. How do we position?

[07:27] Alex: Positioning: focus on predictability + observability. We talk about per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakouts, and rollouts that avoid regressions. Also pricing plug — while others do low list price, hidden costs on caching and burst can erode total cost.

[07:45] Lina: Good. Also demo the Optimize suggestions — batching and quant recommendations — that seems to resonate with infra folks.

[07:53] Priya: I'll include a short Optimize example from a prior customer where batching cut cost 30% without affecting latency SLOs.

[08:02] Alex: Ok, circling back to legal. I'll loop in our partnerships counsel and share the standard co-sell MOU. Lina, Mark — any specific clauses you want?

[08:12] Mark: Simplicity. We want the referral fee clear, the transition to MSA when partners engage in revenue share, and a clause for joint marketing approvals.

[08:21] Alex: Good. I'll send a draft.

[08:25] Lina: Something practical — can we get a playbook line for 'who talks to procurement' and 'who negotiates the SOW'? That gets messy otherwise.

[08:33] Sam: We'll define it: Redwood handles SOW, implementation timelines and pricing; Stratus handles the customer relationship and initial qualification. We'll include a handoff checklist.

[08:42] Ibrahim: On the tech ops — for the on-prem pilot we may need a small agent and infra specs. Priya, can you sketch required VM/GPU profiles?

[08:51] Priya: Yes. I'll share minimal GPU profiles for the models proposed and a recommended env: container images, required ports, and expected disk for KV cache.

[08:59] Alex: Great. Anything else on pipeline rules?

[09:03] Mark: One ask — can Redwood indicate an expected uplift or delta versus existing cloud infra? Our partners like a short ROI statement.

[09:12] Priya: I can draft a one-paragraph ROI example with numbers for a hypothetical 10M monthly token workload — show cost delta and latency improvement.

[09:22] Alex: That'll be helpful.

[09:25] (pause)

[09:37] Sam: Quick admin — I'll set up a bi-weekly sync (30 min) during the sprint and we can escalate ad-hoc for pilots. Does Tues 16:00 UTC work?

[09:45] Mark: Works for us.

[09:48] Lina: Works.

[09:50] Alex: Perfect. I'll send calendar invites for the sprint cadence.

[09:55] Priya: I'll start drafting the benchmark plan and post it to the shared drive.

[10:01] Ibrahim: And I'll prep the sandbox for the on-prem run — expect sample creds by next week.

[10:08] Alex: Recap — action items: Alex share co-sell tracker + MOU, Priya run benchmarks and share runbook/logs, Mark/Lina prioritize opps and provide sample prompts, Ibrahim prepare on-prem sandbox. We've got target due dates in the tracker.

[10:25] Mark: Good meeting. Any objections or blockers?

[10:30] Lina: None here.

[10:34] Sam: Fine.

[10:36] Alex: Alright thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the tracker and with invites.

[10:41] (meeting ends)

References/links mentioned: co-sell tracker (drive link placeholder), Redwood MOU template (link placeholder), Optimize case study (internal doc placeholder)
